data.bottom_line: You can trigger an avalanche large enough to bury you on slopes steeper than about 30 degrees at higher elevations. The most dangerous slopes are those with wind-drifted snow that face west to north through east. If you experience audible collapsing or shooting cracks, give suspect slopes a wide buffer and stick to lower-angle terrain, as you can trigger avalanches from a distance or from below. Slopes less than 30 degrees in wind-sheltered areas and slopes below treeline offer safer travel options.
